inconsistencies: Soft-fork cluster (#35793 BIP54, #31989 CTV, #32247 CSFS, #29247 CAT, #36122 CISA, #35861 Testnet5) was banded unevenly (P1/P2/P3) for the same kind of work: a non-activating or regtest-only consensus implementation. All are now P2 except #36122 (explicit non-merge draft on vendored secp); #35793 leads because it is the only one addressing live consensus vulnerabilities.
Chain: #35861 (Testnet 5) is built on #35793 (BIP 54) and activates its rules from block 1 — review #35793 first; #35861 cannot be evaluated independently.
Chain: #35714 changes flush-failure behaviour and #35731 explicitly builds on it to harden the notification invariant — review #35714 first.
Chain: #35646 is stated to unblock #35570 (returning BlockValidationState directly) — review #35646 first.

Overlapping problem: #29700, #35646, #35003, #36049 and #35714 all rework how fatal/IO errors escape validation and block storage, with #35003 carrying an explicit Approach NACK on exceptions-vs-nullable-returns. These will conflict; the approach decision should be made once (in #35646/#29700) and the behaviour fixes (#35714, #36049, #35003) landed under it.

Same problem, two PRs: #34132 (fatal on point-read/deserialization corruption) and #36280 (throw when a compressed script cannot be decompressed) both stop corrupt database reads being treated as benign. #34132 is the broader change and should be reviewed first.
#32575 is stated groundwork for #29491 (Schnorr batch verification) and also fixes the script-cache bypass in TestBlockValidity — review it before #29491 even though it is a band lower.

Block XOR key pair: #35938 (fail rather than store a null key over a lost one) is the bug fix, #33324 (resumable reobfuscation) is the migration feature; review #35938 first since it prevents the destructive path #33324 only mitigates.

#35569, #36066 and #35906 all feed the stateless validation library (#35904); only #35906 carries substantive validation and test value, the other two are mechanical and should not consume review ahead of it.
#36361 is a backport of already-merged #35168 to 31.x — not duplicate work, but its importance is bounded to that release branch, not to master validation.

assumeutxo/pruning crash cluster (#36346, #35744, #35307, #36452) are the four highest-consequence reliability bugs here and touch overlapping snapshot/pruning state; reviewing them together will be more efficient than in isolation.

#35187 is primarily a libbitcoinkernel API addition that also adds a new ConnectBlock entry path — it is a candidate for the kernel category or for splitting so the validation-side change gets focused review.
#35751 depends on the CoinsViewOverlay from #35295; if that is not yet merged, its dependency must be resolved before review.
result.notes: The category splits cleanly into three groups: concrete chainstate/storage crash-and-corruption bugs (P1 and the top of P2), non-activating consensus/soft-fork implementations whose importance is reaching a correct implementation rather than immediate user impact (middle P2), and internal error-handling/typing refactors plus measured micro-speedups (P3). The main correction applied across the list was banding the soft-fork implementations consistently and promoting the two silent-data-destruction bugs (#35524, #35938) to match the other integrity fixes.
